{{short description|Topology in mathematics}}

In mathematics, the '''inverse bundle''' of a [[fibre bundle]] is its inverse with respect to the [[Whitney sum]] operation.

Let <math>E \rightarrow M</math> be a [[fibre bundle]]. A bundle <math>E' \rightarrow M</math> is called the ''inverse bundle'' of <math>E</math> if their [[Whitney sum]] is a trivial bundle, namely if 

: <math>E \oplus E' \cong M \times \mathbb{R}^n. \, </math>

Any [[vector bundle]] over a [[compact space|compact]] [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]] base has an inverse bundle.
